C++.justification: `int mid(const std::vector<int>& xs){return xs[1];} auto y = mid(xs); return y;`

Go.justification: mid(xs []int32) int32 { return xs[1] }; y := mid(xs); return y. int is a value type so no aliasing after return.

Java.justification: mid(List<Integer> xs){ return xs.get(1); } — returns an autoboxed Integer, a call-site binding, and return of y.

Kotlin.fragment:
fun mid(xs: List<Int>): Int = xs[1]
val xs = listOf(1, 2, 3)
val y = mid(xs)
return y
Kotlin.justification: fun mid(xs: List<Int>): Int = xs[1]; val y = mid(xs); return y.

Python.fragment:
def mid(s):
    return s[1]
xs = [1, 2, 3]
y = mid(xs)
return y
Python.justification: Ordinary function returning xs[1], bound at call site with y = mid(xs); return y is standard.

Quidra.citation: language.md value semantics: array element (scalar) return is a plain value copy; ordinary function/array semantics support this directly.

Quidra.justification: language.md value semantics: array element (scalar) return is a plain value copy; ordinary function/array semantics support this directly.

TypeScript.justification: function mid(a:number[]):number{return a[1];} numbers are primitive value type in JS, y is independent of xs.
